THE GATE READS THIS FILE FROM THE BASE TREE, NEVER FROM THE BRANCH. That is the entire
security model: a branch cannot self-authorize, because the entry that exempts its edit
must already be on main — i.e. it arrived through a PR a human reviewed. Two-PR
discipline, enforced mechanically (Myk, 2026-07-26): first land the authorization here,
An entry exempts a frozen-rail edit ONLY when base + the applicable substitutions is
byte-identical to the branch's file (directly, or after the repo's own prettier). Any
edit beyond the declared substitution is a violation, same as ever.
Shape: { from, to, files?, authorized }. `files` limits the pair to exact paths; an
UNSCOPED pair applies to every frozen rail and must be word-shaped (identifier or quoted
literal) — a SCOPED pair may carry wider literals (a regex fragment, a title phrase)
because the reviewer reads it against the named files. `authorized` names who and when.
Remove entries once the rename that consumed them has merged; a spent entry is inert
(the substitution no longer produces the base) but tidiness keeps this file reviewable.
